title: Decision Ops — Rule Engine Internals and Explainability Logging (working notes)
content:
Purpose:
These are working notes for the Decision Ops / policy evaluation runtime used by the control plane. Focus: how constraints, scoring, and explainability logs are computed and emitted for multi-region routing and runtime fallback. This doc is intentionally pragmatic — perf tradeoffs and data retention considered early.

Scope & assumptions:
- Applies to runtime path that executes policy decisions per-request (route selection, model variant, fallback policy, throttling).
- Evaluation must be low-latency (p95 additional latency budget <= 4ms in most regions).
- Policy definitions are declarative JSON that encode constraints, weights, and metadata; policy artifacts live in control-plane config service (versioned).
- Explainability logs should be compact, privacy-conscious, and indexed for debugging.

High-level architecture:
- Control plane stores policy graphs and exposes the evaluator as an RPC service colocated with regional routing gateways.
- Per-request flow: ingress -> auth -> metadata enrichment -> policy-eval RPC -> routing decision -> send to serving runtime.
- Evaluator implements two phases: (1) constraint evaluation short-circuiting (fast boolean checks), (2) scoring for candidate actions (weights, soft constraints).

Constraint model (fast path):
- Constraint types: hard (must pass), soft_hint (preferred but not blocking), soft_penalty (applies penalty when violated). Examples: region_whitelist (hard), capacity_threshold (soft_penalty), customer_sla_level (hard/soft depending on contract).
- Evaluate hard constraints first; if any fail, remove candidate immediately. Early-exit reduces CPU for scoring phase.
- Constraint indexing: common constraints precompiled into bitmasks for micro-ops (latency optimization).

Scoring model (after constraints):
- Score components are normalized into [0,1] then combined via weighted sum. Components include: latency_estimate_score, cost_score (lower cost -> higher score), freshness_score (model version freshness), reliability_score (recent error rate), affinity_score (customer-region affinity).
- Example formula (pseudocode):
  norm(x) = clamp((x - min) / (max - min), 0, 1)
  final_score = w_lat * norm(1/latency_ms) + w_cost * norm(1/cost_per_token) + w_rel * reliability_score - w_penalty * sum(violation_penalties)
- Weights default per-tenant but can be overridden by rollout policies. We store weight sets as small vectors; evaluator fetches weight vector with policy artifact.

Tie-breaking and deterministic selection:
- If top candidates are within epsilon (0.01), break ties using deterministic hash(customer_id + request_id) against candidate_id to ensure even distribution without oscillation.

Routing policy integration (multi-region):
- Candidate actions include region+zone+model-variant triplets. Routing policy specifies affinity, allowed regions, and fallbacks.
- For multi-region SLOs prioritize region-local candidates then cross-region with cost/risk penalties.
- Cross-region penalty is dynamic: increases with observed inter-region tail latency and decreases if cache/KV prefix is warm.

Explainability logs (design goals):
- Emit compact structured lines per decision containing: request_id, policy_version, chosen_candidate, score_breakdown (component scores as short array), failed_constraints (ids), sampling_flag, latency_us, decision_trace_id. Logs must be queryable and linkable to trace/span.
- Avoid PII: never log raw prompts or user-provided content. Only include stable identifiers (customer_id hashed, request_id truncated).

Proposed explainability log schema (flat fields for fast indexing):
- ts_iso: 2026-02-20T14:22:03.123Z
- decision_trace_id: dt-<uuid>
- request_id: r-<short>
- customer_hash: sha256:abcd1234 (truncate first 12 chars)
- policy_version: v2026-02-19-3
- chosen: region=us-west2|model=redwood-v2q|variant=quant
- scores: [0.83,0.12,0.65,-0.07]  // ordering documented in policy artifact
- constraints_failed: [cap_zone,not_in_whitelist]  // can be empty
- sampling: rate=0.01, seed=42
- eval_latency_us: 320
- rpc_node: cp-usw2-12
- correlation_span: otel-span-id

Sample compact log line (JSON-compact):
{"ts":"2026-02-20T14:22:03.123Z","dt":"dt-9a4","rid":"r-55","cust":"a1b2c3d4e5f6","pv":"v2026-02-19-3","ch":"us-west2|redwood-v2q|quant","sc":"0.83,0.12,0.65,-0.07","cf":"","s":"0.01","lat":320,"node":"cp-usw2-12","span":"abcd"}

Sampling & retention policy for explainability logs:
- Full logs (with score_breakdown) only stored for a small sample (default 0.5%-2% depending on tenant tier). Lean logs (no score array) at higher sampling rate (10%) for telemetry aggregation.
- Retention: full logs kept 30 days for debugging; aggregated/lean logs up to 90 days. Export hooks to cold storage for on-demand longer retention under enterprise agreements.

Privacy & security:
- Any identifier that could be tied to customer identity must be hashed with tenant-specific HMAC salt before logging. Salt rotation documented and enforced by key-management team.
- Explainability export requires RBAC: only SRE/product owners with authorization scope can view unredacted score breakdowns. Audit trail for access.

Performance and cost considerations:
- Constraint bitmask + precompiled scoring micro-kernels reduce evaluator CPU by ~3-4x vs naive JSON walk (benchmarks in linked PR).
- Evaluator caches the last N policy artifacts (N=64) in-memory keyed by tenant to avoid control-plane fetch latency spikes. Cache invalidation via push notifications from control plane when policies change.

Observability & metrics to emit:
- eval.latency_ms (p50/p95/p99), eval.cpu_ms, eval.cache_hit, decisions.per_minute, sampled_logs.emitted, constraint_fail_rate by constraint_id.
- Alert on eval.latency_p95 > 6ms for >5m window.

Operational scenarios / fallbacks:
- If evaluator RPC fails or times out, gateway falls back to a lightweight local policy with conservative defaults (region local, rate-limit, model fallback).
- Staged rollout: feature flags to enable new scoring components; can route small % to new evaluator binary (canary) with shadow logging.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to version weight vectors and ensure warm caches during rollout? (action: Priya to draft versioning protocol by 2026-03-05)
- Sampling strategy: differential sampling for errors vs success — should we upsample when model returns unusual outputs? (action: Ethan to prototype adaptive sampler)
- Confirm retention requirements with Privacy/legal for EU customers (María to sync with compliance).

Action items (short):
- Add deterministic tie-break hash into evaluator core (owner: Anika).
- Implement compact log serializer in Go and a matching parser in observability pipeline (owner: Ethan).
- Document constraint id namespace and register top 30 constraints in Confluence (owner: María).

Notes: these are rough notes for design sync. Keep small and iterative — aim for an MVP that emits compact explainability lines and supports safe rollouts.

References and links: control plane PR above, policy artifact spec in Confluence, Jira RINF-7890 for rollout tracker.

-- End --
